multiple_choice_questions.question: When the content generated by AI completely fails to meet your expectations, you usually:
options: A. Assume the AI is "stupid" and abandon the task.
B. Question if your prompt was imprecise and try rewriting it.
C. Assume there is a system bug or a random error.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When facing a complex task, you prefer to:
options: A. Provide a long, detailed instruction and expect the AI to complete it in one go.
B. Break the task into multiple small steps and guide the AI through a multi-turn conversation.
C. Ask the AI to provide an outline first, then fill in the details step-by-step.

multiple_choice_questions.question: How do you interpret "hallucinations" (false information) provided by AI?
options: A. Intolerable; it indicates the system is completely unusable.
B. Recognize them as a "creative misfire" and correct them through verification.
C. Hard to detect; usually believe the data provided by AI directly.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When the AI uses professional jargon to answer you, your reaction is:
options: A. Very satisfied; it matches my professional background.
B. Confused; ask the AI to switch to plain, easy-to-understand language.
C. Don't mind; only care if the final conclusion is usable.

multiple_choice_questions.question: How do you rate your mastery of Prompt Engineering?
options: A. Proficient; know how to use structured frameworks (e.g., Role, Context, Goal).
B. Knowledgeable; rely mainly on natural language intuition to communicate.
C. Not at all; type randomly as if chatting with a real person.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When a Generative UI dynamically adjusts its layout, you usually:
options: A. Quickly adapt to the new layout and find the functions you need.
B. Feel lost and need time to find the function entry points again.
C. Dislike the change and wish the interface would remain fixed.

multiple_choice_questions.question: If the AI prompts "context length limit reached," your understanding is:
options: A. A technical glitch; I need to refresh the page.
B. The conversation is too long; I need to start a new chat or summarize the previous text.
C. Insufficient storage space; I need to delete files.

multiple_choice_questions.question: For AI-generated images or charts, you value:
options: A. Visual aesthetics and impact.
B. Accurate transmission of data and information.
C. High consistency with my text description.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When you enter a vague command (e.g., "optimize this"), you expect the AI to:
options: A. Automatically guess my intent and provide the result directly.
B. Stop and ask for specific optimization dimensions (e.g., word count, tone, logic).
C. Provide three different versions of optimization for me to choose from.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When processing multimodal information (text, images, code), your focus is on:
options: A. Text logic; others are just auxiliary.
B. Visual presentation; text is just an explanation.
C. The integration of the whole system; focusing on cross-modal consistency.

multiple_choice_questions.question: Do you believe AI can understand your "emotions" or "sarcasm"?
options: A. Believe it can fully perceive them and should provide emotional feedback.
B. Believe it is just simulating probabilities and lacks real understanding.
C. Never consider this; simply treat it as a tool.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When the AI gives a long response, your reading habit is:
options: A. Read every word carefully to ensure no details are missed.
B. Scan quickly for key points like bold text or lists.
C. Scroll directly to the end to read the summary.

multiple_choice_questions.question: How do you understand AI's "creativity"?
options: A. A random combination of existing data fragments.
B. The ability to generate truly unique and inspiring new ideas.
C. Merely mechanical execution of human instructions.

multiple_choice_questions.question: If the AI rejects your request (based on safety policies), you will:
options: A. Understand its boundaries and try to rephrase by bypassing sensitive words.
B. Feel angry and think it is over-censored.
C. Think you did something wrong and stop asking immediately.

multiple_choice_questions.question: Do you understand the purpose of streaming (the typewriter effect)?
options: A. Yes; it allows me to see progress instantly and reduces perceived latency.
B. No; I find the flashing text distracting and prefer the result to appear all at once.
C. No feeling; I've grown accustomed to this presentation.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When faced with automatically generated action buttons in GenUI, you:
options: A. Predict their functions and actively try them out.
B. Ignore them and stick to keyboard input.
C. Carefully read the button labels and click only after confirmation.

multiple_choice_questions.question: How do you distinguish between "Dialogue Mode" and "Creation Mode"?
options: A. Can clearly distinguish the difference in thinking logic between the two.
B. Think there is no difference; both involve typing in a chat box.
C. Rely on visual cues in the interface (e.g., colors, icons) to distinguish.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When the AI shows logical inconsistency, your judgment is:
options: A. It has forgotten the previous conversation context.
B. It is trying to think from different perspectives.
C. Its logical reasoning ability has a ceiling.

multiple_choice_questions.question: How well do you understand the concept of a "Pre-trained Model"?
options: A. Deeply; understand its knowledge cutoff date and the principles of weights.
B. Have heard the term; know it is not connected to the internet in real-time.
C. Completely unfamiliar; think it updates in real-time like a search engine.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When collaborating on code or documents, how do you view the completion suggestions?
options: A. They are a prediction of my thoughts and improve efficiency.
B. They interfere with my train of thought; I prefer to stay in control.
C. They are an authoritative reference; I will adopt them even if I don't understand.

multiple_choice_questions.question: How do you handle contradictory information in AI output?
options: A. Ask the AI again and demand it prove its statement.
B. Use a third-party tool (e.g., Google) for cross-verification.
C. Choose the option that seems more reasonable based on intuition.

multiple_choice_questions.question: Do you understand that AI can play different "Personas"?
options: A. Frequently utilize this; ask it to switch roles for different perspectives.
B. Try it occasionally, but find the effect average.
C. Never use it; consider it just an AI assistant.

multiple_choice_questions.question: How do you understand the "Undo" or "Regenerate" functions in GenUI?
options: A. The only means to correct an AI error.
B. Experimental tools to explore different possibilities.
C. A negative feedback signal indicating dissatisfaction with the current output.

multiple_choice_questions.question: You believe the quality of AI-generated content mainly depends on:
options: A. The model's parameter scale and performance.
B. The quality of the instructions I input (Prompt).
C. The difficulty of the task itself.

multiple_choice_questions.question: Faced with a complex logical diagram generated by AI, your first action is:
options: A. Look for the start and end points to clarify the flow.
B. Look for anomalies or things that contradict common sense.
C. Read the text descriptions next to it before looking at the diagram.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When you first see an AI-generated interface (GenUI), what do you usually do?
options: A. Start using it immediately, figure it out as I go.
B. Browse the overall layout first before starting any operations.
C. Look for help documents or instructions before using it.
D. Compare the interface style with my expectations before deciding how to proceed.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When GenUI automatically adjusts the interface layout for you, how do you judge if the adjustment meets your needs?
options: A. Intuition; if it feels convenient, I accept it.
B. Compare the differences before and after the adjustment and confirm point by point.
C. Try to complete a specific task to see if the result is ideal.
D. Ask others or consult the instructions.

multiple_choice_questions.question: If a functional module you don't recognize appears in the GenUI generated interface, how do you handle it?
options: A. Ignore it and only use the parts I'm familiar with.
B. Click and try it out to see what happens.
C. Hover the mouse or look for tooltip information.
D. Assume there is a problem with the interface and provide feedback to the system.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When the AI-generated interface differs significantly from the style you used previously, what is your first reaction?
options: A. Feel confused; need time to adapt.
B. Feel it's fresh and willing to actively explore.
C. Not adapted; hope to restore the original interface.
D. Don't care; only focus on whether the task can be completed.

multiple_choice_questions.question: How long do you think it takes you to understand the basic logic of a newly generated GenUI interface?
options: A. Less than 1 minute.
B. 1–5 minutes.
C. 5–15 minutes.
D. More than 15 minutes; requires systematic learning.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When GenUI automatically hides certain functions based on your usage habits, are you aware of their existence?
options: A. Yes, I will actively look for hidden content.
B. Sometimes, depending on how familiar I am with the function.
C. Not really; it’s easy to overlook hidden functions.
D. Totally indifferent; functions I don't use are not important.

multiple_choice_questions.question: Facing a dynamically changing GenUI, how do you build a mental model of its overall functions?
options: A. Accumulate understanding gradually through repeated use.
B. Infer function locations based on task goals.
C. Rely on fixed operating habits; do not actively build a model.
D. Learn systematically by consulting documents or tutorials.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When GenUI generates different interfaces for different task scenarios, how quickly can you identify the task type corresponding to the current interface?
options: A. Identify it immediately; the interface change is very intuitive.
B. Need a few seconds of observation before judging.
C. Need to try operating before confirming.
D. Often unable to identify; feel confused.

multiple_choice_questions.question: If a button name in a GenUI-generated interface is different from what you expected, you will:
options: A. Guess its function based on the context.
B. Test it by clicking to confirm the function.
C. Feel confused and pause the operation.
D. Provide feedback to the system regarding the labeling issue.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When using GenUI to complete complex tasks, you are more inclined to:
options: A. Understand the entire process at once before operating.
B. Understand step-by-step; learn while doing.
C. Rely on AI prompts to complete each step.
D. Refer to previous successful experiences and apply them to the new scenario.

multiple_choice_questions.question: Which GenUI interface element do you think helps your understanding the most?
options: A. Visual design of icons.
B. Descriptions of text labels.
C. The position of elements within the interface.
D. The relationship between elements.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When the order of process steps in an AI-generated interface differs from your expectation, you will:
options: A. Operate according to the sequence designed by the AI.
B. Operate according to my own habitual sequence.
C. Understand the AI's design intent before deciding.
D. Feel confused and stop to think.

multiple_choice_questions.question: Which type of GenUI information presentation do you find easier to understand?
options: A. Primarily text-based descriptions.
B. Primarily charts/visualizations.
C. A combination of images and text.
D. Interactive guidance (step-by-step prompts).

multiple_choice_questions.question: When GenUI automatically processes tasks in the background, how do you perceive the progress?
options: A. Through a progress bar or status indicator.
B. Through system notifications or pop-ups.
C. Regularly check the results proactively.
D. Don't pay much attention until the task is completed.

multiple_choice_questions.question: If GenUI generates an interaction pattern you have never seen before, you will:
options: A. Try to operate based on my own intuition.
B. Look for guided prompts or tutorials.
C. Give up using the function.
D. Contact support or consult documentation.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When using GenUI, what situation do you think most affects your understanding of the interface?
options: A. Too many interface elements; high information density.
B. Frequent interface changes; difficult to memorize.
C. Vague functional labels; unclear meanings.
D. Lack of operation feedback; not knowing if it succeeded.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When the GenUI generated structure differs greatly from traditional software you are familiar with, your main way of learning is:
options: A. Autonomous exploration; random attempts.
B. Completing the onboarding guide provided by the system.
C. Observing others' operations or referring to videos.
D. Analyzing the interface logic first, then learning systematically.

multiple_choice_questions.question: How well do you understand GenUI's "Personalized Generation"?
options: A. Clearly know which content is generated specifically for me by the AI.
B. Have a general idea, but the details are unclear.
C. Not quite clear; only know the interface will change.
D. Completely unaware; it’s a "black box" to me.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When multiple optional operation paths appear in the GenUI interface, how do you choose?
options: A. Choose the shortest path.
B. Choose the most familiar path.
C. Operate according to the path recommended by the AI.
D. Weigh the options based on task importance before choosing.

multiple_choice_questions.question: What do you think is the biggest obstacle to your understanding of GenUI?
options: A. Interface changes are too frequent; lack of consistency.
B. The logic of AI-generated content is non-transparent.
C. Personal unfamiliarity with AI technology.
D. The complexity of the task itself.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When using GenUI, how do you usually handle situations where you are unsure if you operated correctly?
options: A. Continue operating to see if the result meets expectations.
B. Undo the operation and start over.
C. Look for confirmation mechanisms (e.g., previews, prompts).
D. Pause and wait for system feedback.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When a function in the GenUI interface does not perfectly match your expected goal, you will:
options: A. Adjust your own goals to adapt to the interface.
B. Try to find an alternative function.
C. Manually request the AI to regenerate the interface.
D. Give up using that function.

multiple_choice_questions.question: Through which way do you prefer to understand the overall structure of a GenUI-generated interface?
options: A. Viewing an interface map or navigation tree.
B. Exploring page by page.
C. Summarizing rules after completing specific tasks.
D. Reading product documentation or instructions.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When GenUI automatically simplifies the interface (reducing options), can you accurately understand the intent behind the simplification?
options: A. Yes, I believe it's to reduce my operational burden.
B. Sometimes, depending on the specific method of simplification.
C. Not really; feel like information is being hidden.
D. Don't pay attention; as long as the result is useful.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When the functional descriptions in GenUI use professional jargon, you usually:
options: A. Infer the meaning based on context.

C. Ignore it and operate directly.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When GenUI generates an interface, how do you usually understand its purpose?

B. Examine components one by one and infer each function.
C. Read text descriptions or labels before trying to understand.
D. Only understand after multiple operations.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When an unfamiliar component appears in the interface, you will:

multiple_choice_questions.question: Faced with a complex GenUI interface, your usual first step is to:

multiple_choice_questions.question: When the interface is inconsistent with your expectations, how do you interpret it?

multiple_choice_questions.question: When GenUI uses abstract icons instead of text, you usually:

multiple_choice_questions.question: When the interface contains multiple functional areas, you prefer to:

multiple_choice_questions.question: When the system-generated interface only partially matches your needs, you will:

multiple_choice_questions.question: When button labels are vague, how do you usually understand them?

multiple_choice_questions.question: When the interface structural hierarchy is deep, you will:

multiple_choice_questions.question: When there is too much information in the interface, you usually:

multiple_choice_questions.question: When the interaction method in the interface is uncommon, you will:

multiple_choice_questions.question: When the layout changes significantly after an interface update, you will:

multiple_choice_questions.question: When there are hidden functions in the interface, you will:

multiple_choice_questions.question: When the interface content changes dynamically, you will:

options: A. Accept them directly.

D. Doubt their rationality.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When the interface supports customization, you will:
options: A. Not use it.

D. Be unsure how to use it.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When multiple input methods appear in the interface, you will:
options: A. Choose the simplest one.

D. Select randomly.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When the interface response is delayed, you will:
options: A. Wait.
B. Repeat the operation.

D. Assume it failed.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When the interface contains auxiliary tips, you will:
options: A. Ignore them.

options: A. Adapt to the system.

C. Follow the prompts.
D. Operate randomly.
